material.excerpt: On this card a bar holds three quarter-note beats. Keep a silent beat’s place even when it ends a bar. The next bar starts on the very next beat.
material.lesson: Use a comfortable three-beat pulse on open A. Continue counting through silence and let the count return to one at the bar line. If playing becomes uncomfortable, stop and trace the bars on paper.

packet.new_task: Count a repeating bar in three. Sustain open A for two beats and leave the third silent. Tap the first beat of the next bar instead of playing it.

packet.shared_work: I bowed open A through counts 1 and 2 and stopped the bow for 3. I tapped when I got to the next 1, then waited through 2 and 3 before starting again on 1. I wasn't sure whether to wait those two beats or start bowing again right after the tap.

response.display: Your written count places the tap on the next 1, where it belongs. Count it like this: “1, 2, silent 3 | TAP on 1.” If you keep the pattern going, the tap replaces the sound on beat 1, so bow on beat 2 and leave beat 3 silent. Waiting through 2 and 3 brings you to the following bar’s 1. Mark that first beat 2 after the tap, replay the phrase once, and listen: did the bow come in on that pulse or on the following 1?
